clue.text: Buzzer in tiny temple arguably for announcement?

indicators.note: for announcement says the made-up word is to be spoken, and what is heard is what goes in the grid

parts.note: a mosque is a temple of sorts, and the Spanish ending -ito marks something small, so a little mosque might arguably be a mosque-ito

explanation.surface: A cryptic musing about a buzzing insect trapped inside a minute shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish diminutive -ito ('little') is tacked onto MOSQUE; 'arguably' admits the coinage is a cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect is named for its whining hum, so a buzzer is a playful description of it.

clue.text: Capital, sharp tool used in action?

parts.note: military action is war
a saw is a toothed cutting tool

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a blade has been put to use in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish city is the seat of government, a national capital.

clue.text: Drunken reveller, driver stopped by officer originally

indicators.note: stopped by means the word for driver is blocked partway by another letter put inside it

parts.note: a driver is a car user

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word officer

explanation.surface: A drunk motorist is pulled over by a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser is someone who drinks and makes merry noisily; a boozy reveller.

clue.text: Star key, look

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
an air is a look or appearance, as in 'an air of confidence'

explanation.surface: Three words that might be a stage direction: the leading performer, a crucial glance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila.

clue.text: All over the place, miss catching ball that's gone up

indicators.note: catching means the word for miss holds another inside it

parts.note: a miss is a young woman, a gal
a lob is a ball hit or thrown high into the air

explanation.surface: A girl at a game, chaotic, grabs a ball lofted skyward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worldwide occurs everywhere, all over the place.

clue.text: See 21
Fast pace cut, time cut back

indicators.note: back means the joined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: to poll is to cut off, as with hair or horns

indicators.note: cut here means the word for time loses its final letter

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A runner's speed is slashed, and the clock is trimmed too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' appears twice with two jobs: first a synonym, then a trimming signal; 'back' then turns POLLAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's fastest gait is a gallop, so it is a quick pace.

clue.text: Common talk a steamy thing on Love Island

parts.note: a fresh cow pat steams in the cold air
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Gossip about a raunchy moment on the reality TV show Love Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British reality dating show; the 'steamy thing' is a cow pat, not a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Patois is the local dialect of ordinary people, everyday speech.

clue.text: Look at artist's uncovered bed, shocked

parts.note: to scan is to look over
Salvador Dali was a surrealist painter, so artist's gives Dali's

indicators.note: uncovered means the word bed loses its top letter, as a bed loses its covers

explanation.surface: Viewers are scandalised by an artist's exposed bed, recalling Tracey Emin's notorious installation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be scandalised is to be outraged or shocked by impropriety.

clue.text: Asians in a queue, say, captivated by bit of a looker

indicators.note: captivated by means the other pieces are held inside the word for part of the eye

parts.note: the iris is part of the eye, which does the looking

indicators.note: say signals the word queue is to be taken by its sound alone

parts.note: a queue is pronounced like the letter Q

explanation.surface: People from Asia standing in line are charmed by a glance from someone attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq lies in western Asia, so its people are Asians.

clue.text: Old couple in the family way rejected, might these take some heat off?

definitions.text: might these take some heat off?

indicators.note: in puts the pair inside the word for the family

parts.note: a clan is a family group

indicators.note: couple says the abbreviation is taken twice, as a pair
rejected means the abbreviation for way is turned round

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: An elderly pair, pregnant, are turned away; perhaps these could cool things down?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the family way' looks like the idiom for pregnant, but 'in' is the insertion signal and 'family' and 'way' are separate synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Coolant fluids carry heat away from engines and machinery.

clue.text: Fairy caught by vampire, pixie in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat says the hidden letters are read backwards
caught by says the letters are held within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fairy is seized by a vampire while a pixie runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Fairy caught' as the definition, but 'caught by' signals the letters held in 'vampire, pixie'; the definition is 'Fairy' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian mythology a peri is a beautiful fairy or sprite.

clue.text: Flatulence offensive, put a knot in it!

parts.note: flatulence is wind
a sortie is a military attack, an offensive

explanation.surface: Someone's gas is an affront, and they are told to tie it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide tie knotted in the broad Windsor style is one to put a knot in.

clue.text: Kindling after log can catch fire

indicators.note: kindling suggests the letters are set burning and broken up, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Once kindling is added to a log, the fire can catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To conflagrate is to burst into flames; a conflagration is a large fire.

clue.text: Farm animal tucking into provender served in a flash?

indicators.note: tucking into means the animal goes inside the word for provender

parts.note: provender is animal food, feed
a lamb is a young sheep on a farm

explanation.surface: A farm animal eats its fodder, dished up fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is flambeed is doused in spirit and set alight, so it arrives in a flash of flame.

clue.text: Furthest behind, I started to crack up

indicators.note: to crack up means the letters break apart and are reassembled

explanation.surface: A lagging runner admits they began to lose their composure.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest to arrive is the most tardy, so the one furthest behind.

clue.text: Prompt perceptible to the audience?

indicators.note: to the audience says the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: anything perceptible is in sight, able to be seen

explanation.surface: A theatre prompt could be noticed by the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like a theatre noun or an adjective, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite someone is to urge or provoke them into action.

clue.text: A heaving of water on top

parts.note: a swell is the rolling heave of the sea

explanation.surface: A surge of sea water rises high.
explanation.definitionFit: On top, meaning besides or additionally, is a synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: Covering article inoffensive?

indicators.note: in puts the article inside the word for offensive

parts.note: insulting is offensive
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of writing that covers a topic is harmless.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulating material wraps around something to cover and protect it.

clue.text: Encourage operator to doff cap

indicators.note: to doff cap means the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a surgeon is someone who operates

explanation.surface: Urge a worker to take off their hat respectfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge on is to spur or cheer someone forward.

clue.text: Free horseboxes for animal involved in a blood sport

definitions.text: animal involved in a blood sport

indicators.note: boxes means the word for horse encloses the other piece

parts.note: a gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
to undo is to free or unfasten

explanation.surface: Horseboxes are released for animals used in hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horseboxes' splits into 'horse' and 'boxes'; GG (gee-gee) is a nursery word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog retrieves game shot by hunters, taking part in a blood sport.

clue.text: Pants one regards where bloomers on display

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Underwear on a washing line, with bloomers on show to the neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like knickers, but means flowers in bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden of rose bushes is a place where flowering plants are shown off.

clue.text: Wrong part of house noted well enough?

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
a gable is the triangular upper part of a house wall

explanation.surface: A badly built part of a house becomes notorious.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that is singable has notes pitched well enough for voices to manage.

clue.text: Caught, famous Smith and Wesson finally turned over

indicators.note: turned over means the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: Delia Smith is a famous British TV cook

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Wesson

explanation.surface: A captured gunman's Smith and Wesson revolver is overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: Smith and Wesson suggests the gunmaker; the Smith is the cookery writer Delia.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nailed is to be caught or exposed, as a criminal is.

clue.text: Missile sees helmsman in river shortly reversing

indicators.note: reversing means the whole assembly is read backwards
in means the steersman sits inside the river's name
shortly means the river's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
a cox steers a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A missile spots a boat's steersman on a river backing away.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'river' is England's Tees; 'reversing' turns TECOXE round. 'sees' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-built Exocet is an anti-ship guided missile.

clue.text: Inspector Lynley's first scrap

parts.note: Inspector Morse is a fictional Oxford detective

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word Lynley's

explanation.surface: TV detective Inspector Lynley's first fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Lynley and Morse are both British TV detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small bit of food, a scrap.
